newsitem.title: FRANCE: French first-half bank profits seen higher.
newsitem.headline: French first-half bank profits seen higher.

text.p: French bank profits are expected to show an improvement in the first half thanks to a sharp rise in revenues from financial market activities, analysts say.
The lone exception will likely be Credit Lyonnais, whose earnings are seen suffering from heavy costs imposed on it as part of its state bailout plans last year.

Analysts surveyed by Reuters said results from traditional banking activities were likely to be poor as a result of a sluggish economy, expected slower growth in consumer lending and lacklustre corporate lending.
Competition on margins remained intense.

But a better performance by the Paris bourse will probably help such banks as Societe Generale reap some capital gains on portfolio disposals with the CAC-40 trading above 2,000 level for much of the first half, analysts said.

Analysts said they expected lower real estate provisions in the first half even if carrying costs remained significant. But they said this improvement would be offset by higher risk charges for small and medium-sized businesses whose bankruptcy rates have risen.
In the cases of Societe Generale and Credit Commercial de France, analysts believe they hit a low point in provisioning last year and do not rule out a slight rise this year.
Here is a forecast of first half results for France's main banking institutions from nine banking analysts polled by Reuters.
- Banque Nationale de Paris. First half due September 12. 1995 first half net attributable profit 996 million Ffr.
Average forecast H1 1996 1.45 billion profit
Highest 1.67 billion Lowest 1.08 billion.
Credit Commercial de France. First half due September 12. 1995 first half net attributable profit 596 million francs.
Average forecast H1 1996 699 million profit
Highest 848 million Lowest 630 million
- Societe Generale. First half due Sept 18. 1995 first half net attributable profit 2.26 billion francs
Average forecast H1 1996 2.57 billion profit
Highest 2.91 billion Lowest 2.3 billion.
Cie Bancaire. First half due Sept 19. 1995 first half net attribuable profit 584 million francs, excluding 253 million francs in exceptionals.
Average forecast H1 1996 298 million profit
Highest 460 million Lowest 223 million
Credit National. First half due Sept 25. 1995 first half net attributable profit before purchase of BFCE 207 million francs.
Average forecast H1 1996 260 million profit
Highest 300 million Lowest 150 million
Credit Lyonnais First half due September 26. 1995 first half net attributable profit 36 million Ffr.
Average forecast H1 1996 1.37 billion francs loss
Highest two billion loss Lowest 800 million loss
Paribas. First half due September 26. 1995 first half net attributable net profit 609 million francs
Average forecast H1 1996 3.35 billion profit
Highest 4.0 billion Lowest 2.0 billion.
NOTE : Analysts say the Paribas forecasts do not carry much significance as the results will include a number of major capital gains on a series of disposals by the bank during the first half.
